ordinary-mon/vigils.html:
Ordinary Time

Vigils

Opening

V. O Lord, open thou my lips. R. And my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.

V. O God, come to my assistance. R. O Lord, make haste to help me.

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Hymn

In the night my soul watcheth for Thee, O God. O Brightness of the Father's face, Immortal Light of Light begone, O Jesus, Saviour of our race, Hear us as we come to thee at dawn.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 129 (130)

In the night my soul watcheth for Thee, O God.

Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice. Let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: Lord, who shall stand it? For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord. My soul hath relied on his word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with him plentiful redemption. And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 1

Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the chair of pestilence. But his will is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he shall meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season. And his leaf shall not fall off: and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper. Not so the wicked, not so: but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth. Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: nor sinners in the council of the just. For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: and the way of the wicked shall perish.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 22 (23)

The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. He hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment. He hath converted my soul. He hath led me on the paths of justice, for his own name's sake. For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff, they have comforted me. Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil; and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it! And thy mercy will follow me all the days of my life. And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord unto length of days.

Reading · Psalm 129:6

""My soul waiteth for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning.""

Responsory

In the night my soul longeth for thee, O God. My spirit within me watcheth for thee.

Collect

Lord of the night watch, as we keep the ancient vigil of thy servants, receive our prayer and grant us at the last to see thy glory undimmed. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

ordinary-mon/lauds.html:
Ordinary Time

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 99 (100)

Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: serve ye the Lord with gladness. Come in before his presence with exceeding great joy. Know ye that the Lord he is God: he made us, and not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Short Reading · Romans 8:26

""The Spirit helpeth our infirmity. For we know not what we should pray for as we ought.""

Responsorium Breve

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Collect

Lord, as light fills this morning, fill us. Let this first hour belong to thee before it belongs to anything else. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

ordinary-mon/vespers.html:
Ordinary Time

Vespers

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Evening Hymn

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 121 (122)

I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord. Our feet were standing in thy courts, O Jerusalem. Jerusalem, which is built as a city, which is compact together. For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord. Peace be in thy strength, and abundance in thy towers. For the sake of my brethren and of my neighbours, I spoke peace of thee.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 126 (127)

Unless the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it. It is vain for you to rise before light, rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow. When he shall give sleep to his beloved. Behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb. As arrows in the hand of the mighty, so the children of them that have been shaken.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 129 (130)

Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice. Let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: Lord, who shall stand it? For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord. My soul hath relied on his word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with him plentiful redemption.

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Short Reading · 1 Peter 5:7

""Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

Grant us, Lord, an evening free from care, and a night of peaceful rest. As this day has been given for thy praise, so may the night renew us for the work of thy kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Salve Regina · Marian Antiphon

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

ordinary-mon/compline.html:
Ordinary Time

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Night Psalm · Psalm 4

When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me. Have mercy on me: and hear my prayer. Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him. Be ye angry, and sin not: the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds. In peace in the selfsame I will sleep, and I will rest: For thou, O Lord, singularly hast settled me in hope.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Short Reading · 1 Peter 5:8

""Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Collect

Visit this place, O Lord, and drive far from it all snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to keep us in peace; and let thy blessing be always upon us. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Salve Regina · Marian Antiphon

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 99 (100)

Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: serve ye the Lord with gladness. Come in before his presence with exceeding great joy. Know ye that the Lord he is God: he made us, and not we ourselves. The Lord is my light and my salvation.

To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Lord, as light fills this morning, fill us. Let this first hour belong to thee before it belongs to anything else. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

Ordinary Time

Vespers

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Evening Hymn

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 121 (122)

I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord. Our feet were standing in thy courts, O Jerusalem. Jerusalem, which is built as a city, which is compact together. For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord. Peace be in thy strength, and abundance in thy towers. For the sake of my brethren and of my neighbours, I spoke peace of thee.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 126 (127)

Unless the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it. It is vain for you to rise before light, rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow. When he shall give sleep to his beloved. Behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb. As arrows in the hand of the mighty, so the children of them that have been shaken.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 129 (130)

Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice. Let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: Lord, who shall stand it? For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord. My soul hath relied on his word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with him plentiful redemption.

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Short Reading · 1 Peter 5:7

""Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

Grant us, Lord, an evening free from care, and a night of peaceful rest. As this day has been given for thy praise, so may the night renew us for the work of thy kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Salve Regina · Marian Antiphon

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

ordinary-sun/compline.html:
Ordinary Time

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Night Psalm · Psalm 90 (91)

He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob. He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: my God, in him will I trust. For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the sharp word. He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust. Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flieth in the day.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Short Reading · 1 Peter 5:8

""Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Collect

Visit this place, O Lord, and drive far from it all snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to keep us in peace; and let thy blessing be always upon us. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Salve Regina · Marian Antiphon

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.

ordinary-solemnity/lauds.html:
Ordinary Time

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 99 (100)

Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: serve ye the Lord with gladness. Come in before his presence with exceeding great joy. Know ye that the Lord he is God: he made us, and not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

Short Reading · Romans 8:26

""The Spirit helpeth our infirmity. For we know not what we should pray for as we ought.""

Responsorium Breve

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Collect

Lord, as light fills this morning, fill us. Let this first hour belong to thee before it belongs to anything else. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

ordinary-solemnity/vespers.html:
Ordinary Time

Vespers

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Evening Hymn

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 121 (122)

I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord. Our feet were standing in thy courts, O Jerusalem. Jerusalem, which is built as a city, which is compact together. For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord. Peace be in thy strength, and abundance in thy towers. For the sake of my brethren and of my neighbours, I spoke peace of thee.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 126 (127)

Unless the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it. It is vain for you to rise before light, rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow. When he shall give sleep to his beloved. Behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb. As arrows in the hand of the mighty, so the children of them that have been shaken.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 129 (130)

Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice. Let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication. If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: Lord, who shall stand it? For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord. My soul hath relied on his word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with him plentiful redemption.

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Short Reading · 1 Peter 5:7

""Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, O Lord.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

Grant us, Lord, an evening free from care, and a night of peaceful rest. As this day has been given for thy praise, so may the night renew us for the work of thy kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Salve Regina · Marian Antiphon

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

ordinary-solemnity/compline.html:
Ordinary Time

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Night Psalm · Psalm 90 (91)

He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob. He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: my God, in him will I trust. For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the sharp word. He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust. Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flieth in the day.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Short Reading · 1 Peter 5:8

""Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.

Collect

Visit this place, O Lord, and drive far from it all snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to keep us in peace; and let thy blessing be always upon us. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Salve Regina · Marian Antiphon

Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.

advent-sun/lauds.html:
Advent

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Come, Lord Jesus. Do not delay.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 62 (63)

O God, thou art my God: I will watch for thee at the break of day. For thee my soul hath thirsted; for thee my flesh, O how many ways! In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory. For thy mercy is better than lives: thee my lips shall praise. Thus will I bless thee all my life long: and in thy name I will lift up my hands. Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips. If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

Come, Lord Jesus. Do not delay.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Come, Lord Jesus. Do not delay.

Short Reading · Romans 13:12

""The night is past and the day is at hand. Let us put off the works of darkness.""

Responsorium Breve

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Collect

Stir up thy power, O Lord, and come. With great might succour us, that through thy grace and mercy the swift approach of thy Son may find us neither sleeping nor afraid. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

advent-sun/vespers.html:
Advent

Vespers

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Evening Hymn

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 109 (110)

The Lord said to my Lord: Sit thou at my right hand: until I make thy enemies thy footstool. The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: rule thou in the midst of thy enemies. With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: from the womb before the day star I begot thee. The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 110 (111)

I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; in the council of the just, and in the congregation. Great are the works of the Lord: sought out according to all his wills. His work is praise and magnificence: and his justice continueth for ever and ever. He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. His praise continueth for ever and ever.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 111 (112)

Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments. His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the righteous shall be blessed. Wealth and riches shall be in his house: and his justice remaineth for ever and ever. He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: his horn shall be exalted in glory.

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

Short Reading · Malachi 3:1

""Behold, I am sending my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

Stir up our hearts, O Lord, to prepare the ways of thine only-begotten Son, that through his coming we may be found worthy to serve thee with purified minds. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Alma Redemptoris Mater · Marian Antiphon

Alma Redemptoris Mater, quae pervia caeli porta manes, et stella maris, succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo: tu quae genuisti, natura mirante, tuum sanctum Genitorem, Virgo prius ac posterius, Gabrielis ab ore sumens illud Ave, peccatorum miserere.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

advent-sun/compline.html:
Advent

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Night Psalm · Psalm 90 (91)

He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob. He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: my God, in him will I trust. For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the sharp word. He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust. Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flieth in the day.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Short Reading · Revelation 3:11

""Behold I come quickly. Hold fast that which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Collect

Lord Jesus, who art to come to judge the living and the dead: enlighten the darkness of our hearts with thy grace, that we may be ready when thou comest. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Alma Redemptoris Mater · Marian Antiphon

(Loving Mother of the Redeemer -- traditional Advent and Christmas antiphon)

Alma Redemptoris Mater, quae pervia caeli porta manes, et stella maris, succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo: tu quae genuisti, natura mirante, tuum sanctum Genitorem, Virgo prius ac posterius, Gabrielis ab ore sumens illud Ave, peccatorum miserere.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.

advent-wed/lauds.html:
Advent

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Come, Lord Jesus. Do not delay.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 62 (63)

O God, thou art my God: I will watch for thee at the break of day. For thee my soul hath thirsted; for thee my flesh, O how many ways! In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory. For thy mercy is better than lives: thee my lips shall praise. Thus will I bless thee all my life long: and in thy name I will lift up my hands. Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips. If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

Come, Lord Jesus. Do not delay.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Come, Lord Jesus. Do not delay.

Short Reading · Romans 13:12

""The night is past and the day is at hand. Let us put off the works of darkness.""

Responsorium Breve

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Collect

Stir up thy power, O Lord, and come. With great might succour us, that through thy grace and mercy the swift approach of thy Son may find us neither sleeping nor afraid. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

advent-wed/vespers.html:
Advent

Vespers

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Evening Hymn

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 109 (110)

The Lord said to my Lord: Sit thou at my right hand: until I make thy enemies thy footstool. The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: rule thou in the midst of thy enemies. With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: from the womb before the day star I begot thee. The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 110 (111)

I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; in the council of the just, and in the congregation. Great are the works of the Lord: sought out according to all his wills. His work is praise and magnificence: and his justice continueth for ever and ever. He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. His praise continueth for ever and ever.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 111 (112)

Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments. His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the righteous shall be blessed. Wealth and riches shall be in his house: and his justice remaineth for ever and ever. He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: his horn shall be exalted in glory.

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

Short Reading · Malachi 3:1

""Behold, I am sending my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Behold, the Lord shall come, and all his saints with him.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

Stir up our hearts, O Lord, to prepare the ways of thine only-begotten Son, that through his coming we may be found worthy to serve thee with purified minds. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Alma Redemptoris Mater · Marian Antiphon

Alma Redemptoris Mater, quae pervia caeli porta manes, et stella maris, succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo: tu quae genuisti, natura mirante, tuum sanctum Genitorem, Virgo prius ac posterius, Gabrielis ab ore sumens illud Ave, peccatorum miserere.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

Advent

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Night Psalm · Psalm 4

When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me. Have mercy on me: and hear my prayer. Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him. Be ye angry, and sin not: the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds. In peace in the selfsame I will sleep, and I will rest: For thou, O Lord, singularly hast settled me in hope.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Short Reading · Revelation 3:11

""Behold I come quickly. Hold fast that which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

The Lord will come and will not delay.

Lord Jesus, who art to come to judge the living and the dead: enlighten the darkness of our hearts with thy grace, that we may be ready when thou comest. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

christmas-fri/lauds.html:
Christmas

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Today Christ is born; today the Saviour has appeared.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 62 (63)

O God, thou art my God: I will watch for thee at the break of day. For thee my soul hath thirsted; for thee my flesh, O how many ways! In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory. For thy mercy is better than lives: thee my lips shall praise. Thus will I bless thee all my life long: and in thy name I will lift up my hands. Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips. If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

Today Christ is born; today the Saviour has appeared.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

""God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all hath spoken to us by his Son.""

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Collect

O God, who hast made this day sacred by the birth of thy Son: grant that we who receive him as Redeemer may behold him with joy when he comes as Judge. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

Antiphon

Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 109 (110)

Psalm 2 · Psalm 111 (112)

Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments. Wealth and riches shall be in his house: and his justice remaineth for ever and ever. He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 127 (128)

Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: that walk in his ways. For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee. Thy wife as a fruitful vine, on the sides of thy house. Thy children as olive plants, round about thy table. Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.

Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.

Short Reading · Titus 2:11

""The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

O God, who hast made this night radiant with the brightness of the true Light: grant that we, who have known the mystery of that Light on earth, may enter into the fullness of his joys in heaven. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Alma Redemptoris Mater, quae pervia caeli porta manes, et stella maris, succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo: tu quae genuisti, natura mirante, tuum sanctum Genitorem, Virgo prius ac posterius, Gabrielis ab ore sumens illud Ave, peccatorum miserere.

christmas-fri/compline.html:
Christmas

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

God sent his Son into the world to save the world.

Night Psalm · Psalm 4

When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me. Have mercy on me: and hear my prayer. Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him. Be ye angry, and sin not: the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds. In peace in the selfsame I will sleep, and I will rest: For thou, O Lord, singularly hast settled me in hope.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

God sent his Son into the world to save the world.

Short Reading · Titus 2:11-12

""The grace of God our Saviour hath appeared to all men, instructing us to live soberly.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

God sent his Son into the world to save the world.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

God sent his Son into the world to save the world.

Collect

O God, who hast gladdened us by the birth of thy Son: grant that thy light, which hath enlightened us this day, may guide our steps through the darkness of this night. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Alma Redemptoris Mater · Marian Antiphon

(Loving Mother of the Redeemer -- traditional Advent and Christmas antiphon)

Alma Redemptoris Mater, quae pervia caeli porta manes, et stella maris, succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo: tu quae genuisti, natura mirante, tuum sanctum Genitorem, Virgo prius ac posterius, Gabrielis ab ore sumens illud Ave, peccatorum miserere.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.

Lent

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Create in me a clean heart, O God.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 5

Give ear, O Lord, to my words, understand my cry. Attend to the voice of my prayer, O my King and my God. For to thee will I pray: O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice. In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

Create in me a clean heart, O God.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Create in me a clean heart, O God.

""We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.""

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

O Lord our God, grant us the grace to begin this day in penitence and to end it in praise, that through thy mercy the labours of this holy season may bear fruit in our lives. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

Lent

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 112 (113)

From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise. The Lord is high above all nations; and his glory above the heavens. Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth? Who raiseth up the needy from the earth, and lifteth up the poor from the dunghill.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 115 (116):10-19

I have believed, therefore have I spoken; but I have been humbled exceedingly. I said in my excess: Every man is a liar. What shall I render to the Lord, for all the things that he hath rendered to me? I will take the chalice of salvation; and I will call upon the name of the Lord. I will pay my vows to the Lord before all his people: precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 116 (117)

O praise the Lord, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people. For his mercy is confirmed upon us: and the truth of the Lord remaineth for ever.

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

Short Reading · Joel 2:13

""Return to the Lord, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

O Lord, as this day draws toward its close, receive our evening prayer. Turn our hearts ever more completely toward thee throughout the remaining days of this holy season. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Ave Regina Caelorum · Marian Antiphon

Ave, Regina caelorum, Ave, Domina angelorum: Salve, radix, salve, porta, ex qua mundo lux est orta. Gaude, Virgo gloriosa, super omnes speciosa; Vale, O valde decora, et pro nobis Christum exora.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

lent-sun/compline.html:
Lent

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Night Psalm · Psalm 90 (91)

He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob. He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: my God, in him will I trust. For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the sharp word. He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust. Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flieth in the day.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Short Reading · Matthew 24:13

""He that shall endure to the end, he shall be saved.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Collect

Be our light in the darkness, O Lord, and in thy great mercy defend us from all perils and dangers of this night. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Ave Regina Caelorum · Marian Antiphon

(Hail, O Queen of Heaven -- traditional Lenten antiphon)

Ave, Regina caelorum, Ave, Domina angelorum: Salve, radix, salve, porta, ex qua mundo lux est orta. Gaude, Virgo gloriosa, super omnes speciosa; Vale, O valde decora, et pro nobis Christum exora.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.

lent-thu/lauds.html:
Lent

Lauds

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Create in me a clean heart, O God.

Morning Psalm · Psalm 62 (63)

O God, thou art my God: I will watch for thee at the break of day. For thee my soul hath thirsted; for thee my flesh, O how many ways! In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory. For thy mercy is better than lives: thee my lips shall praise. Thus will I bless thee all my life long: and in thy name I will lift up my hands. Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips. If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning.

Canticle · Benedictus · Zechariah 1:68-79

Create in me a clean heart, O God.

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people. And hath raised up a horn of salvation to us, in the house of David his servant. As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning. Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us. To perform mercy to our fathers, and to remember his holy testament. The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us. That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear, In holiness and justice before him, all our days. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest; for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins. Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in which the Orient from on high hath visited us. To enlighten them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Create in me a clean heart, O God.

Short Reading · 2 Corinthians 6:1

""We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.""

Responsorium Breve

The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven. And his kingdom shall rule over all.

Collect

O Lord our God, grant us the grace to begin this day in penitence and to end it in praise, that through thy mercy the labours of this holy season may bear fruit in our lives. Through Christ our Lord.

Amen.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

lent-thu/vespers.html:
Lent

Vespers

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Evening Hymn

O blest Creator of the light, Who mak'st the day with radiance bright, And o'er the forming world didst call The light from chaos first of all: Whose wisdom joined in meet array The morn and eve, and named them Day: Night comes with all its darkling fears; Regard thy people's prayers and tears.

Antiphon

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

Psalm 1 · Psalm 109 (110)

The Lord said to my Lord: Sit thou at my right hand: until I make thy enemies thy footstool. The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: rule thou in the midst of thy enemies. Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

Psalm 2 · Psalm 111 (112)

Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments. Wealth and riches shall be in his house: and his justice remaineth for ever and ever. He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

Psalm 3 · Psalm 127 (128)

Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: that walk in his ways. For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee. Thy wife as a fruitful vine, on the sides of thy house. Thy children as olive plants, round about thy table. Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

Short Reading · Joel 2:13

""Return to the Lord, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love.""

Responsorium

Our heart hath rejoiced in him, because we have hoped in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.

Magnificat · Canticle of Our Lady · Luke 1:46-55

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Behold, now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.

Intercessions

Lord, as evening falls, we bring before thee the prayers of thy people. For those who labour in darkness -- grant them light. For those who suffer alone -- send them consolation. For those who have died this day -- receive them into thy peace. For the Church throughout the world -- preserve her in truth. Lord, have mercy.

Collect

O Lord, as this day draws toward its close, receive our evening prayer. Turn our hearts ever more completely toward thee throughout the remaining days of this holy season. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Ave Regina Caelorum · Marian Antiphon

Ave, Regina caelorum, Ave, Domina angelorum: Salve, radix, salve, porta, ex qua mundo lux est orta. Gaude, Virgo gloriosa, super omnes speciosa; Vale, O valde decora, et pro nobis Christum exora.

Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

lent-thu/compline.html:
Lent

Compline

Examination of Conscience

Pause briefly. Call to mind the faults of this day.

I confess to Almighty God, and to you my brothers and sisters, that I have sinned through my own fault, in my thoughts and in my words, in what I have done and in what I have failed to do; and I ask Blessed Mary ever Virgin, all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

Have mercy on us, O Lord. For we have sinned against thee.

Opening

O God, come to my assistance. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Antiphon

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Night Psalm · Psalm 90 (91)

He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob. He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: my God, in him will I trust. For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the sharp word. He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust. Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flieth in the day.

Psalm 133 (134) · Night Praise

Behold now bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, and bless ye the Lord. The Lord out of Sion bless thee, he that made heaven and earth.

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Short Reading · Matthew 24:13

""He that shall endure to the end, he shall be saved.""

Responsorium

Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. V. For thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth. R. I commend my spirit.

Nunc Dimittis · Canticle of Simeon

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love.

Collect

Be our light in the darkness, O Lord, and in thy great mercy defend us from all perils and dangers of this night. Through Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

Ave Regina Caelorum · Marian Antiphon

(Hail, O Queen of Heaven -- traditional Lenten antiphon)

Ave, Regina caelorum, Ave, Domina angelorum: Salve, radix, salve, porta, ex qua mundo lux est orta. Gaude, Virgo gloriosa, super omnes speciosa; Vale, O valde decora, et pro nobis Christum exora.

Blessing

May the all-powerful Lord grant us a restful night and a peaceful death. R. Amen.
